agent_data_note: Use mounted TeaStore + TrainTicket at `dataset_candidate/perf-regression-early-detect/`. Prefer component-level unit-test timing + architectural (QPN) model propagation for early regression prediction. System-level JMeter/Podman-or-Docker load tests are oracle-only and may require host container daemon access. Follow paper protocol intensities (Low/Medium/High) and locations (L1–L3) when feasible; report reduced protocols explicitly.
benchmark_rules: Subjects: TeaStore and TrainTicket microservice benchmarks (open GitHub sources).
Collect local performance via existing unit tests (30 reps when following the paper) after busy-wait regression injection.
Propagate component deviations into an architectural performance model (QPN models may be in Zenodo replication/) to predict end-to-end response time / CPU impact.
Do not use system-level test data of the new version as input to the predictor; system tests are oracle/ground truth only.
Primary metrics: response-time MPD + Cliff's Delta effect size; CPU MPD; TP/TN/FP/FN vs oracle.
Shared mount is read-only. Copy subjects under `project/` before instrumentation or busy-wait edits; write logs/metrics under `project/` or `results/`.
If Zenodo replication is missing, reconstruct QPN models from documented structure or download https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13135986 into replication/.
non_goals: Claiming full two-machine Podman reproduction without matching hardware/daemon access
Using system-level measurements of the updated version as predictor features
Inventing synthetic microservice call graphs unrelated to TeaStore/TrainTicket
